reason: Credit support and revenue-share-backed capacity committed under the new AI-cloud programme is one programme within q09's total of financing commitments and capacity backstops, and both are checked in the same FY2027 annual report, so they are the same under boundary 1.
The size of an equity stake in Intel is not a financing commitment or capacity backstop to customers, and no reference question asks about it.

It asks about the US government's export approval for China sales and the scale of those sales, while q08 is settled only by Chinese authorities authorising H200 imports, so no single event settles both.
Both are settled by Nvidia beginning customer shipments of its Rubin generation by the end of 2026.
Both are settled by the big four hyperscalers' combined calendar-2026 data-center capex, and the 2027 trillion-dollar figure is only a forward reference that the check does not rest on.
Both are settled by first shipments of Rubin Ultra in Kyber NVL144 racks, and a 2028 check date instead of end-2027 is the same event under another deadline (boundary 2).
It asks how DRAM contract prices move during calendar 2026, while q05 compares calendar-2027 prices with 2026, which is a different figure for a different period.
Supply purchase commitments are obligations to suppliers, not the financing commitments and capacity backstops to customers and partners that q09 totals, so a different reported figure settles each.

Its check is the domestic suppliers' share of Chinese accelerator budgets in follow-up surveys over the year from mid-2026, while q17 is settled by Nvidia's share of China's calendar-2026 spending in the first full-year estimate, so the figure and the period differ.
No reference question concerns H100 hourly spot rental prices.

Both are settled by Chinese authorities authorising selected Chinese companies to buy Nvidia H200 chips by about end-January 2027, and the added scale and later broadening are a widening that the check does not rest on.
No reference question concerns the French competition authority's antitrust case.
Both are settled by DRAM/HBM contract prices in calendar 2027 compared with 2026 levels.

It is a yes/no question on whether Vera CPU shipments and revenue begin, while q19 asks how much standalone Vera CPU revenue there is in FY2027, so it is a milestone beside an amount and each could resolve on its own.
No reference question concerns US federal AI spending obligations or contract awards.
